title: Prediction input contract
story: As an API client, I want invalid inputs to be rejected clearly so that I can fix my request.
acceptance_criteria: AC-101-1: Values at the bounds of every field are accepted. | AC-101-2: A value just outside a bound, or of the wrong type, returns 422 and names the field. | AC-101-3: An empty body is valid: every field has a default. | AC-101-4: An invalid request returns 422 even when no model is loaded.

title: Prediction responses
story: As an API client, I want a predictable answer in every situation.
acceptance_criteria: AC-102-1: A valid request with a model loaded returns 200 and a predicted fare. | AC-102-2: Without a model the API returns 503 and never loads a model during the request. | AC-102-3: An error raised by the model returns 500. | AC-102-4: A successful prediction updates the prediction and revenue counters.

title: Request correlation and logs
story: As an on-call engineer, I want to follow one request across logs and traces.
acceptance_criteria: AC-103-1: The `X-Request-ID` sent by the client is returned unchanged. | AC-103-2: Without one, the API generates a 32-character hexadecimal id. | AC-103-3: Logs are JSON lines with the documented fields. | AC-103-4: Payload values never appear in logs.

title: Readiness
story: As an operator, I want `/health` to tell whether the service can really predict.
acceptance_criteria: AC-104-1: Without a model, `/health` returns 503. | AC-104-2: With a model that cannot predict, `/health` returns 503. | AC-104-3: With a working model, `/health` returns 200 with the version and a smoke fare.

title: Delayed feedback
story: As a data scientist, I want real fares to update the online error.
acceptance_criteria: AC-105-1: Feedback bodies outside the documented bounds return 422. | AC-105-2: Only the last 10,000 predictions can receive feedback; the oldest is forgotten first. | AC-105-3: A prediction receives feedback once; unknown, expired or used ids return 404. | AC-105-4: Accepted feedback returns the error and updates the error counters.

title: Fault injection and metric labels
story: As an operator, I want fault injection to be safe and metrics to stay bounded.
acceptance_criteria: AC-106-1: Fault injection is refused unless explicitly enabled. | AC-106-2: Injected latency appears in its own span. | AC-106-3: Unknown paths are labelled `unmatched` in metrics.

title: Data preparation
story: As a data engineer, I want raw trips to become clean features.
acceptance_criteria: AC-107-1: Source columns are renamed to the internal names. | AC-107-2: A missing required column fails with its name. | AC-107-3: `pickup_weekday` is 1 from Monday to Friday and 0 at the weekend. | AC-107-4: `total_fare` adds the optional components, counting absent ones as 0.

title: Data validation and quarantine
story: As a data engineer, I want bad rows set aside, never lost, and a broken source to stop the pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: AC-108-1: Rows outside the valid ranges are quarantined with a reason. | AC-108-2: Quarantined rows keep a readable reason. | AC-108-3: More than 20% invalid rows fails the preparation; exactly 20% passes. | AC-108-4: Fewer than 100 valid rows fails the preparation; exactly 100 passes. | AC-108-5: Ingesting the same source twice does not duplicate rows.

title: Drift detection
story: As a data scientist, I want drift to be decided by documented thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: AC-109-1: Two identical samples have a PSI of 0 and no drift. | AC-109-2: A feature drifts when PSI or KS reaches its threshold (threshold included). | AC-109-3: The dataset drifts when the share of drifted features reaches its threshold (threshold included). | AC-109-4: Thresholds come from the configuration file, not from the code.

title: Training and promotion
story: As a data scientist, I want a new model to replace the champion only when it is better.
acceptance_criteria: AC-110-1: Candidate and champion are scored on the same validation data. | AC-110-2: The candidate is promoted only if its error is strictly lower; a tie keeps the champion. | AC-110-3: The champion alias moves only after all artifacts are stored.

title: Alert rules
story: As an on-call engineer, I want alerts that fire for the right reason and tell me what to do.
acceptance_criteria: AC-111-1: Thresholds, durations and severities match the specification. | AC-111-2: During an outage of the API, only the root cause is notified. | AC-111-3: Every alert has a summary, a description, an action and a runbook link.

title: Supporting services
story: As an operator, I want the support services to be safe and bounded.
acceptance_criteria: AC-112-1: The alert receiver keeps at most 200 notifications, newest first. | AC-112-2: The controller can only stop or start the prediction API. | AC-112-3: The load simulator rejects settings outside their bounds.

title: Fast enough API
story: As a product owner, I want the API to be fast enough for our users.
acceptance_criteria: AC-113-1: The API responds fast enough.

title: Retrain when data changes
story: As a product owner, I want the model to be retrained when the data changes a lot.
acceptance_criteria: AC-114-1: A significant data change triggers a retraining.

title: Protect the admin endpoints
story: As a security officer, I want the admin endpoints to be protected.
